questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & \frac{10}{3} \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & \frac{10}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=\frac{10}{3} \\  & y=-\frac{5}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-\frac{5}{3}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-\frac{5}{3})=\frac{10}{3}\,⇒\,x=\frac{10}{3}-\frac{10}{3}=0.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=0$ and $y=-\frac{5}{3}.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 8 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+5y=-6 \\  & -6x-6y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -6 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -6 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-8 \\  & 2x+4y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 10 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-8 \\  & y=2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(2)=-8\,⇒\,x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=2.$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 12 & -4 \\ 5 & 11 & 3\end{aligned}].

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -8 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y=0 \\ y=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+2(1)=0 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\left<  -2,1 \right>.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+5y=5 \\ x-6y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & -1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5y=-5 \\ y=-10,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-10$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-5(-10)=-5 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-55.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-55$ and $y=-10.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -55,-10 \rangle.$
